title: Global menu items disappear when a pop-up window opens, but don't show up again after it closes
line: The Global Menu no longer goes empty when an app opens a dialog, and the app's menus are still there after the dialog closes.
explanation: On Wayland, opening a dialog first deactivates the main window, so the task model reports no active task and the Global Menu empties. The dialog then appears already active, and the task model makes its parent (the main window) the active task again, but only by setting a variable without emitting dataChanged; the Global Menu (and anything else following activeTask) never learned about it, and when the dialog closed the parent was already the active task so nothing changed either. The change emits the IsActive change when a newly added window makes a different task active, as the existing activation handler already does.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: notify when a window appears already active

A new window that is already active, such as a dialog, made its leader
the active task without telling anyone, so the Global Menu stayed empty
after the dialog closed. Emit the IsActive change for it, too.

BUG: 483075

media.caption: Master: LibreOffice Writer (XWayland). The menu empties when Find and Replace opens and stays empty after it closes and after clicking the document, although Writer's task is active.
With the fix: the same steps; Writer's menus stay in the Global Menu throughout.
Master: Find and Replace open, Global Menu empty.
With the fix: Find and Replace open, Global Menu still shows Writer's menus.
Master: open Find and Replace with Ctrl+H, close it with Esc, click the document.
With the fix: the same run.

review.text: Strong root-cause fix in the right layer (WaylandTasksModel::Private::addWindow): when a transient dialog appeared already active after its parent deactivated, activeWindow was reassigned to the leader without emitting dataChanged(IsActive), leaving TasksModel::activeTask and Global Menu stuck empty even after the dialog closed. Emitting IsActive mirrors the existing activeChanged handler, safely no-ops when effectiveActive is the not-yet-inserted window itself, and is backed by clear before/after media and passing libtaskmanager autotests.

reviews.text: Strong root-cause fix in the right layer (WaylandTasksModel::Private::addWindow): when a transient dialog appeared already active after its parent deactivated, activeWindow was reassigned to the leader without emitting dataChanged(IsActive), leaving TasksModel::activeTask and Global Menu stuck empty even after the dialog closed. Emitting IsActive mirrors the existing activeChanged handler, safely no-ops when effectiveActive is the not-yet-inserted window itself, and is backed by clear before/after media and passing libtaskmanager autotests.

This finds the real cause in libtaskmanager. When a transient appears already active, addWindow made its leader the active window without emitting IsActive, so activeTask users (the Global Menu, the task manager) never saw the leader become active again. The fix copies what the existing activeChanged handler already does, and it is a no-op for a new top-level window that isn't in the rows yet. The before/after strips match the reporter's LibreOffice case and the regression checks are reasonable. The remaining ordering case (leader deactivated after the dialog is added) is pre-existing and noted honestly.
